SUMMARY

Danaher Corporation(DHR+3.53%)reported third quarter results that exceeded internal projections for revenue, earnings, and cash flow, driven by improving end market trends and strong commercial execution. Management identified four strategic priorities for the company's next phase of growth: commercial excellence, innovation, talent, and disciplined capital allocation. The company reported robust underlying demand across large pharma and biopharma customers, while biotechnology activity continued to strengthen. Management stated that the portfolio transformation into a specialized Life Sciences and Diagnostics company is largely complete, shifting focus toward delivering higher core growth and gaining market share. Integration of recent acquisitions, including Masimo and StatLab, is progressing as the company seeks strategically compounding opportunities to enhance its laboratory and clinical workflows.

Operator:My name is Chelsea, and I will be your conference facilitator this morning. At this time, I would like to welcome everyone to Danaher Corporation's third quarter 2026 earnings results conference call. All lines have been placed on mute to prevent any background noise. After the speakers' remarks, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question during that time, simply press star then the number one on your telephone keypad. If you would like to withdraw your question, please press star two. I will now turn the call over to Ms. Rachel Vatnsdal, Vice President of Investor Relations. Ms. Vatnsdal, you may begin your conference.

Rachel Vatnsdal:Good morning, everyone, and thanks for joining us on the call. With us today are Julie Sawyer Montgomery, our President and Chief Executive Officer, and Matt Gugino, our Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. I'd like to point out that our earnings release, quarterly report on Form 10-Q, the slide presentation supplementing today's call, the reconciliations, and other information required by SEC Regulation G relating to any non-GAAP financial measures provided during the call, and a note containing details of historical and anticipated future financial performance are all available on the investors section of our website, www.danaher.com, under the heading Quarterly Earnings.

The audio portion of this call will be archived on the investors section of our website later today under the heading Events and Presentations and will remain archived until our next quarterly call. A dial-in replay of this call will also be available until November 4th, 2026. During the presentation, we will describe certain of the more significant factors that impacted year-over-year performance. Our Form 10-Q and the supplemental materials I referenced describe additional factors that impacted year-over-year performance. Unless otherwise noted, all references in these remarks and supplemental materials to company-specific financial metrics relate to results from continuing operations in the third quarter of 2026, and all references to period-to-period increases or decreases in financial metrics are year-over-year.

We may also describe certain products and devices which have applications submitted and pending for certain regulatory approvals or are available only in certain markets. During the call, we will make forward-looking statements within the meaning of our federal securities laws, including statements regarding events or developments that we believe or anticipate will or may occur in the future. These forward-looking statements are subject to a number of risks and uncertainties, including those set forth in our SEC filings, and actual results may differ materially from any forward-looking statements that we make today.

These forward-looking statements speak only as of the date that they are made, and we do not assume any obligation to update any forward-looking statements except as required by law. With that, I'd like to turn the call over to Julie.

Julie Sawyer Montgomery:Thank you, Rachel, and good morning, everyone. Before we get into the quarter, I'd like to share my perspective on Danaher today and the opportunity ahead as I begin this next chapter as CEO. The opportunity for Danaher is straightforward: to become the defining leader in Life Sciences and Diagnostics, a company that unambiguously gains share, delivers sustainable, profitable growth, and helps our customers improve outcomes for patients around the world. The foundation we built at Danaher is strong. We operate leading businesses, foster deep customer relationships, and empower talented people, all enabled by the Danaher Business System. At the same time, growth over the past several years has not consistently reflected the full potential of our portfolio.

We've navigated significant changes in our markets, but regardless of the environment, we hold ourselves to a higher standard. We see a meaningful opportunity to accelerate sustainable core revenue growth, gain share more consistently, and more fully translate the strength of our portfolio into differentiated performance. I'm confident in what we've built, and I'm energized by what I've seen across Danaher these last few months. Our focus now is strengthening execution and delivering on that potential. Recently, I had a conversation with one of our executives preparing for a customer meeting related to Alzheimer's disease.

What started as a discussion about how one of our businesses could help address a particular part of that customer's challenge quickly expanded to cover the roles seven different operating companies could play across discovery, AI-enabled target selection, laboratory automation, process development, scale-up, and diagnostic testing. When the challenge is Alzheimer's disease, speed matters, both to the scientists working to understand it and the families waiting for answers. That conversation reinforced something important. Our customers don't think about their challenges through the lens of our organizational structure. They have a problem to solve, and they want the best partnership and solutions we can bring them.

I see this as critical to Danaher's next chapter, as some of our greatest opportunities sit at the intersections of our businesses. We will preserve what makes our operating company structure advantage, the customer intimacy, the accountability, while making it easier to bring the full power of Danaher to our customers. Our foundation and the power of the Danaher Business System have given us leadership positions across the Life Sciences and Diagnostic markets and a unique role in helping accelerate the translation of scientific discovery into human impact. Our Life Science businesses enable discovery, our Biotechnology businesses help turn those discoveries into scaled and accessible therapies, and our Diagnostics businesses help guide treatment.

Together, Danaher spans a broad path from experiment to patient with DBS adding speed and operating discipline at scale. We call that innovation at the speed of life, helping close the distance between human need and the science that answers it. As we enter this next chapter, we'll accelerate that ambition by focusing on four strategic priorities: commercial excellence, innovation, talent, and effective capital allocation. Each is important, but our most immediate opportunity is commercial execution. Danaher has successfully repositioned its portfolio with three platforms across the Life Sciences and Diagnostics markets. With that portfolio transformation largely complete, our focus is shifting from reshaping the portfolio to delivering more growth from the businesses we own.

We will focus our leadership attention on exceptional commercial execution, enhancing our pursuit of unambiguous share gain across Danaher. We will drive consistency and rigor and commercial execution across our businesses. This means simplifying and strengthening our commercial processes and empowering our leaders to make more entrepreneurial decisions. We also have an opportunity to make it easier for our customers to take advantage of the full power of Danaher. Our operating companies have important brands and deep customer relationships. These will remain fundamental to how we compete, but Danaher has tremendous scale and breadth, and we can do more to use that advantage. That means making the broader strength of our portfolio and capabilities more accessible to customers.

We have already taken practical steps to show up as a more connected Danaher. In Diagnostics, for example, we are successfully deepening customer relationships by bringing leaders from across our businesses together with key customers to look across the portfolio, better understand their priorities, and identify where a more coordinated approach can create additional value. We do this by having our key Diagnostics leaders in the same room at the same time with our key customers to understand their biggest pain points and where we can drive incremental value. This approach has generated meaningful incremental revenue opportunities and is helping drive share gains across our Diagnostics businesses.

As we bring more of Danaher to our customers, we can also become more systematic about connecting capabilities across our businesses to solve more customer needs. Aldevron and Cytiva's recent collaboration to deliver an end-to-end mRNA solution is a great example, helping streamline our customers' development processes while meaningfully accelerating timelines. Ultimately, our commercial strategy is straightforward. Execute better and more entrepreneurially, show up together as Danaher for our customers, and connect our capabilities where we can create greater value. We will make it easier for customers to access the full strength of Danaher and look to us when trying to solve their most important challenges. Our second priority is delivering more innovation.

Danaher is already at the forefront of innovation, but I believe strengthening our innovation capabilities represents one of our largest opportunities to accelerate long-term growth. Delivering on our brand promise, innovation at the speed of life, means we will be deliberate and strategic about where we invest in R&D and ensure we appropriately allocate resources behind our best ideas. That means more closely linking strategy and R&D investments, concentrating resources behind the highest potential initiatives, and working more closely across our businesses and external partners to move promising innovations faster. We will also fund transformational opportunities at the enterprise level when we believe Danaher has a clear right to win and larger investment can create meaningful competitive advantage.

These decisions will require clear choices and greater enterprise-level conviction about where we can create the most value. Innovation cycles take time, but over the long term, we believe this more focused approach can support higher and more durable core revenue growth while turning more scientific discoveries into meaningful human impact. To me, this is the heart of innovation at the speed of life, helping promising science move faster towards the patients who need it. Our third priority is being the home and destination for exceptional talent. We believe our ability to attract and develop exceptional talent in scientific, AI, commercial, and operating disciplines will increasingly set us apart from competitors.

We also need to develop and deploy our people more intentionally against Danaher's highest priority growth and innovation opportunities. Danaher has given me that kind of exposure in my own career, learning DBS and then applying it across commercial, R&D, and business leadership. I want us to continue to create exceptional opportunity for the next generation of leaders. As we evolve DBS for the AI era, I believe we can create an even more compelling place for the best talent in our industry. Our fourth priority is being more disciplined with our capital and resources. M&A and capital deployment have been essential drivers of Danaher's growth and will remain so.

We will maintain the robust investment criteria that has served us well for many decades while bringing strategic clarity and discipline to how we allocate capital and resources. We are focused on deepening our positions in attractive markets and identifying strategically compounding areas that build from the strengths we already have in our businesses. Our objective is to deliver high returns on our investments with greater consistency while positioning Danaher for sustainably differentiated and profitable growth. Across each of these priorities, there is a common idea. We create more value by building a stronger, more connected company. That doesn't mean changing what makes our operating companies successful.

It means preserving their customer intimacy and accountability while making it easier to share ideas, capabilities, talent, and resources across Danaher, and using our scale where it gives us an advantage. AI is one capability we believe can help us do just that. We believe the combination of AI and DBS will be an important competitive advantage. DBS gives us a common way to solve problems, improve processes, and scale what works across Danaher. We believe that approach can help us bring AI solutions to life faster and more effectively than many.

Over time, we believe AI can make DBS simpler and more powerful while DBS can help us implement AI with the rigor and consistency that have long defined Danaher. We see opportunities for AI to strengthen commercial execution and innovation. For example, helping our teams identify opportunities earlier, improve sales funnel management, and dramatically reduce R&D timelines. AI can help simplify work and drive greater productivity. AI isn't only about making Danaher better. It is also changing the needs of our customers and creating new opportunities across our portfolio. For example, we see growing demand for solutions that cut across our Life Sciences businesses that enable more automated and autonomous labs and workflows.

We also see longer-term opportunities across our Biotechnology and Diagnostics platforms to make therapies more efficiently and make treatment decisions more precisely. This is why we are accelerating AI deployment across the enterprise and establishing AI partnerships. Stepping back, we believe a more connected Danaher with a stronger focus on commercial excellence, innovation, and talent can be a stronger Danaher. We intend to bring the best of Danaher to our customers to better leverage our talent, platforms, and brand, and simplify how we operate so our teams can focus on the opportunities that matter most. Together, these actions can help us move faster and more fully realize the potential of our portfolio. I am incredibly excited about what lies ahead.

We are starting from a position of strength with meaningful room to deliver more. That will take time, and we know credibility will be earned through results. Our focus now is making clear choices about where we invest and executing with greater speed and consistency. We believe that can accelerate profitable growth, drive share gains, and most importantly, help our customers improve outcomes for patients around the world. With that, let me turn to our third quarter results. Our third quarter came in ahead of our expectations on both the top and bottom line, with Biotechnology, Life Sciences, and Diagnostics core revenue, excluding respiratory revenue, all growing mid-single digits or better.

Core revenue growth, excluding respiratory revenue, improved to 5.5%, and we delivered a nearly 30% adjusted operating profit margin. These results reflect both improved end market conditions and the benefit of strong commercial and operational execution across the portfolio. We're particularly encouraged by the improved momentum we saw across our businesses. Underlying demand across large pharma and biopharma remained robust. Biotech activity continued to strengthen. While academic demand remained below historic levels, demand improved sequentially. Meanwhile, clinical and applied end markets remained healthy and continued to perform well. Having spent considerable time with our teams over the past several weeks, I've seen firsthand the talent, innovation, and customer focus that make Danaher unique.

Let me walk you through a few notable examples from across Danaher this quarter. During a recent visit to Cytiva's site in Uppsala, Sweden, I had the opportunity to spend time with the teams developing and manufacturing some of our industry-leading products. Seeing firsthand the depth of science and engineering behind these technologies reinforced my confidence in our competitive position. I was particularly impressed by the process development team and how closely that team works side by side with customers to solve their most difficult challenges. That partnership has long been important in traditional monoclonal antibodies, and it becomes even more valuable as our customers move towards more complex molecules and modalities.

We're bringing innovation and process expertise to help customers solve those challenges, and importantly, we're seeing that differentiated approach help us win more specifications with customers. Next, we recently announced our first AI-powered autonomous lab. Based at Abcam, this lab brings together AI, robotics, and technologies from across our portfolio, including Cytiva, Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, Genedata, IDT, and Molecular Devices, to offer a connected design, make, and test workflow.

By continuously learning from each experiment, the platform is designed to help researchers move from idea to validated reagent up to eight times faster, while generating up to ten times higher volume compared to existing models, helping accelerate scientific discovery while providing the rigorous quality and reproducibility required to advance AI-driven drug discovery. Our partnership with NVIDIA, announced last week, will further advance this vision by connecting our instruments and workflows with NVIDIA's capabilities to help shape autonomous science for our customers. On the capital allocation front, Leica Biosystems closed the acquisition of StatLab in early Q4.

StatLab strengthens Leica's value proposition by enabling a more complete pathology workflow while advancing our integrated delivery network strategy and helping clinicians diagnose cancer faster and more precisely. We're very pleased to welcome the StatLab team to Danaher. Finally, Masimo, our other recent acquisition, continued to track ahead of our initial expectations and delivered another quarter of high single-digit revenue growth. Having spent time with the team just last week, the integration is progressing well across the business with a healthy funnel of cost savings and commercial synergy opportunities.

The team has also continued to innovate at an impressive pace, recently receiving FDA clearance for its smartSET platform that can help detect atrial fibrillation, a common heart rhythm disorder that often goes undetected and significantly increases the risk of stroke. This technology can help patients earlier who may benefit from further medical evaluation and care. I want to congratulate the Masimo team for their sixth FDA clearance this year and for extending the value of their technology beyond monitoring to help detect important clinical conditions like atrial fibrillation. With that, I will turn the call over to Matt, who will walk you through our Q3 results and guidance in more detail.

Matt Gugino:Thanks, Julie, and good morning, everyone. As Julie stated, we delivered a solid third quarter with better than expected growth, earnings, and cash flow. Sales were $6.6 billion and core growth, excluding respiratory revenue, was up 5.5%, an encouraging 100 basis points acceleration from the second quarter and a continuation of the improvement we have seen throughout the year. Respiratory revenue, while slightly better than expected, represented an approximately 250 basis point headwind in the quarter, resulting in core revenue growth of 3%. Geographically, core revenues in developed markets were flat. Western Europe grew mid-single digits and North America was down low single digits, primarily driven by lower respiratory revenue.

Core revenues in high growth markets increased approximately 10% with healthy growth across all major regions. China was up high single digits with growth in all three of our segments. Biotechnology and Life Sciences were supported by healthier funding and investment levels, and Diagnostics continued to move beyond the most significant impacts of China's healthcare policy changes. Our gross profit margin for the third quarter was 58.5%. Our adjusted operating profit margin of 29% was up 110 basis points and exceeded expectations, driven primarily by strong operational execution with a modest benefit from tariff refunds received during the quarter. Adjusted diluted net earnings per common share of $2.11 were up approximately 11.5%.

We generated $1.6 billion of free cash flow in the quarter and $4 billion in the first three quarters of the year, resulting in a year-to-date free cash flow to net income conversion ratio of 128%, further underwriting the differentiated quality of our earnings. Now turning towards our business segments. Core revenue in our Biotechnology segment increased 5%. Core revenue in discovery and medical decreased low single digits with solid growth in protein research instrumentation more than offset by timing and lab consumables. Core revenue in bioprocessing grew towards the upper end of mid-single digits, modestly better than our expectations. Consumables were up mid-single digits, led by upstream consumables, while equipment increased low single digits.

Orders grew mid-teens in the quarter, with particular strength in both upstream consumables as well as reagents. There is no change to our full year expectation of mid-single digit core revenue growth from bioprocessing. Demand trends remain healthy across the business, supported by strong commercial production activity and a robust pipeline of new programs. These underlying market trends, combined with Cytiva's differentiated portfolio, deep scientific expertise, and recent innovations, reinforce our confidence in the business' ability to deliver sustainable high single digit long-term revenue growth while helping customers improve yields, increase manufacturing efficiency, and scale new therapies. Turning to our Life Sciences segment, core revenue increased 4.5%.

Core revenue in Pall's applied filtration business increased mid-single digits, driven by continued robust growth in aerospace and microelectronics. Core revenue in our Life Sciences instruments businesses increased mid-single digits in the quarter. SCIEX led the way with strong demand from pharma and biopharma customers, a modest improvement in U.S. academic spending, and continued momentum for new products such as ZenoTOF 8600. Beckman Coulter Life Sciences also delivered strong results, including in automation, where the team has seen increased demand for AI-enabled solutions and services.

Core revenue in our Life Sciences consumables businesses collectively grew low single digits in the quarter, driven by continued momentum in IDT's MRD and next generation sequencing product lines, while Abcam saw improved academic demand and solid traction from pharma and biopharma commercial initiatives. Moving to our Diagnostic segment, core revenue growth excluding respiratory revenue was up 7%. Respiratory revenue was an approximately 650 basis point headwind in the quarter, resulting in core revenue growth of 50 basis points. Core revenue in our clinical Diagnostics businesses increased mid-single digits in the quarter. We saw notable performance at Leica Biosystems, with particular strong momentum in digital pathology as well as advanced staining.

Beckman Coulter Diagnostics also delivered its highest core growth quarter in more than two years. The traction we saw from new product introductions, including the DxI 9000, together with easing China policy related headwinds, reinforces our confidence in Beckman's competitive position and ability to accelerate their growth trajectory. In molecular diagnostics, core revenue in Cepheid's non-respiratory business increased low double digits, led by growth in group A strep, virology, and sexual health assays. Respiratory revenue was approximately $350 million in the third quarter, down year-over-year, due primarily to lower global infection rates, but modestly ahead of our expectations as we saw customers purchase ahead of the upcoming respiratory season.

Now let's turn to our fourth quarter and full year 2026 outlook and give you an initial perspective on how we're thinking about 2027. In the fourth quarter, we expect core revenue growth excluding respiratory revenue to be in the 4%-5% range. We expect respiratory revenue to be an approximately 150 basis point headwind. Additionally, we expect a fourth quarter adjusted operating profit margin of approximately 29.5%. For the full year 2026, we are increasing our full year adjusted diluted net EPS guidance to $8.57-$8.62 versus our prior range of $8.45-$8.60. This reflects the benefit of our third quarter outperformance and represents double digit year-over-year EPS growth.

Turning to 2027, while it's still too early to provide a formal outlook, we want to give you some perspective on how we're thinking about core growth next year. We're encouraged by the improvement in the end markets and the growth we've delivered throughout 2026. Excluding respiratory revenue, core revenue growth has averaged 4%-5% over the past several quarters. As we look to 2027, we think that 4%-5% core revenue growth, excluding respiratory revenue, is the right starting point as we sit today. We will provide a more quantitative and detailed guidance outlook in January, but hopefully this gives you a helpful starting point for how we are thinking about next year.

With that, I will turn the call back over to Julie.

Julie Sawyer Montgomery:Thanks, Matt. To wrap up, we are pleased to deliver better than expected third quarter results and encouraged by the improving growth trends we saw across the business. As I reflect on my first few weeks as CEO, the time I have spent with our teams and customers has only strengthened my conviction in the solid foundation Danaher has built. My focus now is simple: create more value for customers, accelerate innovation, attract and develop great talent, and deploy capital in ways that strengthens Danaher for the long term. These priorities are designed to drive faster and more durable core growth, deliver unambiguous share gains, and more fully translate the strength of our portfolio into differentiated performance.

While realizing the full potential of these opportunities will take time, I am confident that with DBS as our foundation, we are uniquely positioned to turn those opportunities into results for our customers and the patients they serve, our associates, and our shareholders. I am excited about what we can accomplish together and the results we can deliver as we continue building an even stronger Danaher. With that, I will turn the call back over to Rachel.

Rachel Vatnsdal:Thanks, Julie. That concludes our formal comments. We are now ready for questions.

Operator:Thank you, Rachel. At this time, if you would like to ask a question, please press star one on your keypad. To leave the queue at any time, please press star two. We ask that you please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. Once again, that is star one to ask a question. Our first question will come from Doug Schenkel with UBS. Please go ahead.

Doug Schenkel:Hi. Good morning. Thank you for taking my questions. Julie, welcome to the call. As the new CEO, you are new to the role, but as we all know, you are certainly not new to Danaher. Recognizing that, and also that this has been a challenging period for the company, but also that Danaher has a legacy of operational excellence and solid capital deployment, how are you balancing the legacy of a company that has business school case studies written about its strategy and execution versus the opportunity and need to make change? Essentially, as you sit here today, what is foundational, and how do you think about evolving the playbook?

Julie Sawyer Montgomery:Doug, thank you, and thank you for the thoughtful question. Danaher is a great company and one I am incredibly proud to lead. We have a great heritage with HBS case studies written about us, and I know exactly what you are referring to, as I read that case study when I decided to join Danaher nine years ago. We also have truly unique differentiators that continue to serve us well today. Exceptional talent, a great portfolio, and a continuous improvement culture supported by a business system that is unparalleled. At the same time, as I said in my prepared remarks, we have an opportunity to grow at a higher rate than we have in recent years.

When I talk to our teams, I say that unambiguous share gain is our true report card. I want to preserve what makes us great, but also ensure we are focused on the most important priorities for who we are today. Let me break that down a bit. You heard me talk about becoming a more connected Danaher. When that Harvard case study was written, our businesses were lower growth markets and our customers typically bought from a single operating company. We are in a very different situation today. Higher growth, scientific markets with the same customers buying across three, six, 12 operating companies. We will keep the advantages of our operating company structure in place.

I think of that as the accountability, the customer and technical intimacy, and the unique development opportunities for our people. But we will also work in a more connected way that makes it easier for customers to access the full power of Danaher. I still talk to customers who are surprised to learn that company XYZ is part of Danaher, and yet we are a strategic partner to those customers. These customers are inevitably interested in a broader conversation that can lead to higher share of wallet for us and better solutions for the customer. That same thinking, ensuring we are focused on what matters most for the company we are today, extends to our other priorities.

You heard me say we will focus more on commercial excellence. Now that we are in a growthier market, more leadership focus on commercial prowess leads to more value creation. I also spoke about strategy-led innovation. This is important because our markets today are fueled by scientific discovery. As a result, we need to know where the puck is going and to make focused, higher impact investments. And talent. For this age and these markets, we need to develop and attract the best AI, science, technology, and operating talent to innovate at the speed of life.

We will want to continue to focus on capital allocation while ensuring we do so in strategically compounding ways to help the flywheel of our businesses turn better and faster. So what you hear me saying is, I don't view these priorities as a generic playbook, but as what best enables us to become that defining leader now that we are a fully scaled Life Sciences and Diagnostics company.

Doug Schenkel:Thanks for that, Julie. One follow-up on your prepared remarks from earlier on the call. You outlined several priorities. What's the biggest one that you expect to have the greatest impact over the near term, say, over the next 12-18 months? What operating or financial metrics should investors use to assess progress pursuant to that top priority?

Julie Sawyer Montgomery:Sure. Step one is really prioritizing aligning our teams around accelerated profitable growth and unambiguous share gain as the report card, and that's what our investors should be looking for. That leads to a clear near-term opportunity to further drive commercial excellence across the enterprise. This means being super clear on simple but powerful expectations for our sales team and what leaders will drive and inspect. Frankly, this is where DBS creates a real advantage for us. What will then further accelerate this is when we consistently show up as a more connected Danaher. There are pockets across the business where this is working extremely well.

I mentioned we've seen a lot of success with this in Diagnostics where we started to speak to customers as diagnostic solutions in addition to individual operating companies. This has led to much more senior and strategic dialogues and value propositions that have created several hundred millions of dollars of opportunity in a short time. We are also seeing this in our Life Sciences approach to the new tech bios, and we have approached these AI native drug development companies this way from the start, and I really like the traction we are seeing.

One of the things I have been pleased to learn over the course of my transition to CEO is that when I talk to customers across all three of our platforms, they want to see more of this from us. These changes will take some time, but our report card is higher core growth, profitable core growth, and unambiguous share gain.

Operator:Thank you. Our next question will come from Vijay Kumar with Evercore ISI. Please go ahead.

Vijay Kumar:Hi, guys. Good morning, and thank you for taking my question. Julie, congratulations to you. I guess, my first question, Matt, I think you made some helpful comments here on the fiscal 2027 framework. I am curious, when I look at your bioprocessing segments, came in quite solid here in 3Q, and you have a few moving pieces into 2027, and the instrument orders have been quite solid here year-to-date. You could see some activity from onshoring. You do have a catch-up from this order push-out in consumable. I am curious, should bioprocessing be pushing very high singles, low double digits, when you think about fiscal 2027?

Matt Gugino:Yeah, Vijay. Thanks for the question here. I think just to start with bioprocessing here for 2026 and how we feel like we are going to finish the year. No change to our full year expectations for 2026 for bioprocessing, mid-single digit core growth. We saw Q3 was actually a bit better than we expected, the upper end of that mid-single digit range. From an orders perspective, they remain strong. Mid-teens order growth that was led by upstream consumables as well as resins. Given order trends and those order trends that we are seeing, we would expect to see bioprocessing growth rates continue to improve in 2027. We gave that overall Danaher outlook of 4%-5% core growth ex respiratory.

As we want to get through our planning processes and as we'll do with the rest of our businesses, we want to see how Q4 shapes up here before we provide more formal guidance, whether it's around bioprocessing or the other segments here. All in, good to see the order trajectory, view bioprocessing long term as a high single digit growth business and encouraged by what we're seeing.

Julie Sawyer Montgomery:Vijay, I can add a little bit of color here, because as you would imagine, this is a place where I've spent quite a bit of time recently, both with the team and with customers. My conclusion is we have a differentiated portfolio with the most comprehensive offering in bioprocessing. This really positions us to win with virtually any customer across nearly every step of the workflow. We like the secular drivers. There's a record number of monoclonal antibodies coming to market, the acceleration of biosimilars, and newer modalities like the antibody drug conjugates, cell therapy, the bi-trispecifics are adding to the volume, and of course, the reshoring opportunity.

As I meet with customers, it is clear they value us as a critical partner and not just a supplier. They bring to us their most critical problems, and we are very good at solving them. All in, very confident that bioprocessing is a high single digit business here over the long term, as Matt said.

Vijay Kumar:That's helpful, Julie. Maybe one for you on capital deployment. Love to hear your views on capital deployment. You come from Diagnostics. We've seen a couple of acquisitions within that segment. How are you thinking of M&A opportunities and areas of interest for Danaher? The reason I ask on areas of interest is, Masimo, is that kind of signaling a more med tech tilt, if you will, or how are you thinking of areas of priorities?

Julie Sawyer Montgomery:Yeah. Thanks, Vijay. M&A remains our bias for capital allocation as we think it is the best way to compound returns over the long term, and we are going to continue to look for strategically compounding M&A. Of course, we will keep a robust investment criteria that has served us well for decades. We see Masimo, and just recently here, StatLab, as good examples of this. I see opportunities to strengthen all three of our platforms, both organically and inorganically through M&A. You talk about Masimo. I actually do not see that as a med tech M&A play. I see it as a continuous diagnostic that is strategically compounding with our Diagnostics business.

We already see the commercial synergies at work, and we are able to have scientific conversations around how the combination of continuous monitoring and biomarkers can lead to better outcomes for patients. Just another example of something that we view as strategically compounding. There is certainly no bias here to med tech.

Operator:Thank you. Our next question comes from Tycho Peterson with Jefferies. Please go ahead.

Tycho Peterson:Hey, thanks. Matt, I want to stress test the assumptions you put out for next year, the 4%-5%. I have a lot of people asking why you are not accelerating here. Appreciate your comments on bioproduction a minute ago. You had the order resin delays, obviously, in biotech, that should come through. You do not have the China VBP headwind. You have recovering biotech, academic picking up a bit. So, why on earth would ex-respiratory be the same? I think you kind of alluded to the fact you just want to see how 4Q shapes up, and 4%-5% is maybe a 4%, but maybe get us comfortable there is something that you are not baking in that is getting worse.

Julie Sawyer Montgomery:Hey, Tycho, this is Julie. As Matt discussed, we've delivered core growth ex respiratory in the 4%-5% range the last few quarters, so we think that's a reasonable starting point for 2027 based on the current end market conditions. I'm only a few weeks into the CEO role, but the time I spent with our teams and customers has certainly reinforced my confidence in our positioning and the improving end markets. I am going to ask the same exact question around M&A, because clearly in Danaher's 50-year history, there is a long history of very successful M&A, and there has been a few stinkers in there, obviously, that have impacted your portfolio of late. Do you feel the need to change the process? Again, I will ask it in kind of the same way, process over the people. Do you change how you work the funnel? How do you drive to that lower risk, higher consistency, higher return kind of mandate and still put capital to work?

Because I have seen other companies— Yeah. —go through these stages, and they kind of freeze. They become afraid to do deals because they are afraid to make a mistake. So how do you keep that flywheel moving so that you are putting capital to work, but increase your hit rate from here?

Julie Sawyer Montgomery:Yeah, no, thank you for the question. We certainly don't want to freeze. Capital allocation remains a priority for us. Frankly, we have great processes and great teams for M&A. You mentioned some that haven't performed as well in the recent past, and I think as a company, we have learned from that. Our focus is really just ensuring that we're doing strategically compounding M&A with a robust return profile. If you look at our recent deals, obviously, it's early days, but I think that they will be strong returns for us and strategically compounding.

Operator:Thank you. Our next question will come from Casey Woodring with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Casey Woodring:Great. Thank you for taking my questions. Julie, looking forward to working with you. Maybe a follow-up to an earlier question, but just on Masimo, you talked a little bit about how you view the business fitting into Danaher, and you obviously led that deal as Head of Diagnostics. Maybe can you just walk through the current trends you're seeing in that business and how we should think about Masimo contribution next year?

Julie Sawyer Montgomery:Yeah, thank you for the question. Masimo is off to a great start. They delivered high single digits here in Q3, their first full quarter as part of Danaher, and year-to-date as well. I was just with the team last week. The integration is progressing extremely well. They've already completed in sustainment for over 10 Kaizens with more planned along the way. Frankly, it's just tremendously rewarding to work with that team and see them get excited about DBS, how the lean thinking can support a better cost position, better on-time delivery for the customers. We have a healthy funnel of the commercial synergies that we were anticipating. In true Danaher fashion, we will also learn from Masimo.

We're extremely impressed by their rate of innovation and some of their commercial techniques as well, and that's always been part of what makes Danaher stronger.

Casey Woodring:Understood. That's helpful. Then, maybe as a follow-up, you called out mid-teens order growth in bioprocessing. If you could maybe just double-click on the equipment piece of that order growth, maybe parse out how much pent-up demand you're seeing over the last several quarters. Then would also be curious to hear on reshoring as well, kind of what you're seeing from an order perspective there and how reshoring could potentially contribute to growth in 2027. Thank you.

Matt Gugino:Sure, Casey. I'll take the order growth part of the question, then kick it over to Julie for reshoring. So another quarter of mid-teens order growth overall in bioprocessing. That was led by upstream consumables as well as resins. Encouraged by those trends, continue to build backlog here. Also, when you think about equipment versus consumables orders year-to-date, both up nicely with those equipment orders continuing in that strong double-digit range. So really supportive of those improving end market and underlying trends in the business.

Julie Sawyer Montgomery:Yes. Casey, on reshoring is playing out largely as we expected. We're seeing some brownfield activity today, and that has a modest impact to our order book at the moment. Those larger greenfield projects are still in the planning phases. The funnel and quoting activity is beginning to pick up, but we see that as more of a 2028 plus event in terms of when it starts to hit the P&L. We do think this is a strong opportunity ultimately for the business, and it could be a billion-dollar market opportunity in the U.S. But as I said, we'll expect it to play out across several years, mostly starting in 2028.

Operator:Thank you. Our last question will come from Evie Koslosky with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Evie Koslosky:Great. Thank you for squeezing me in. Julie, congrats on the new role. Within Life Sciences, maybe walk through the key end markets of where we are in the recovery within academic and then biotech, but maybe specifically within emerging biotech, and then also within industrial and semis. What are you hearing from customers in terms of where they are with spending versus kind of where we still have room in the recovery and any areas that investors should look for potential acceleration and levers for upside into next year?

Julie Sawyer Montgomery:Great. Thank you, Evie, for the question. You saw here in Q3, we grew 4.5% and finished above our expectations, driven by the improving end markets and the traction on some recent commercial initiatives, as well as some new product launches. Frankly, this is the third quarter in a row where Life Sciences has beat our internal expectations. The end markets continue to steadily improve. Large pharma and biopharma remained robust. Biotech funding is reading through. Academic demand, still below historic levels, but improved modestly sequentially. We saw continued strength in clinical and applied markets, including in MicroE at Pall.

Our customers, they are really interested, and we're starting to see some of that early demand for the AI-driven workflow solutions, and that's first starting to show up in automation at Beckman Life Sciences. As I mentioned, I think we're very well positioned here in AI. Customers like the breadth of our portfolio, and we will turn that into a value proposition for them that's around ease of integration through common standards across the instruments.

Operator:Thank you. We have now reached our allotted time for questions, and I would like to turn the call back over to Rachel for any additional or closing remarks.

Rachel Vatnsdal:Perfect. Thank you, Operator. Thank you, everyone, for joining us today this morning. We will be around the rest of the day and the week for follow-ups if any of you have questions. Thank you.

Operator:Thank you, ladies and gentlemen. This brings us to the end of today's meeting. We appreciate your time and participation, and you may now disconnect.

Operator:My name is Chelsea, and I will be your conference facilitator this morning. At this time, I would like to welcome everyone to Danaher Corporation's third quarter 2026 earnings results conference call. All lines have been placed on mute to prevent any background noise. After the speakers' remarks, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question during that time, simply press star then the number one on your telephone keypad. If you would like to withdraw your question, please press star two. I will now turn the call over to Ms. Rachel Vatnsdal, Vice President of Investor Relations. Ms. Vatnsdal, you may begin your conference.

Rachel Vatnsdal:Good morning, everyone, and thanks for joining us on the call. With us today are Julie Sawyer Montgomery, our President and Chief Executive Officer, and Matt Gugino, our Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. I'd like to point out that our earnings release, quarterly report on Form 10-Q, the slide presentation supplementing today's call, the reconciliations, and other information required by SEC Regulation G relating to any non-GAAP financial measures provided during the call, and a note containing details of historical and anticipated future financial performance are all available on the investors section of our website, www.danaher.com, under the heading Quarterly Earnings.

The audio portion of this call will be archived on the investors section of our website later today under the heading Events and Presentations and will remain archived until our next quarterly call. A dial-in replay of this call will also be available until November 4th, 2026. During the presentation, we will describe certain of the more significant factors that impacted year-over-year performance. Our Form 10-Q and the supplemental materials I referenced describe additional factors that impacted year-over-year performance. Unless otherwise noted, all references in these remarks and supplemental materials to company-specific financial metrics relate to results from continuing operations in the third quarter of 2026, and all references to period-to-period increases or decreases in financial metrics are year-over-year.

We may also describe certain products and devices which have applications submitted and pending for certain regulatory approvals or are available only in certain markets. During the call, we will make forward-looking statements within the meaning of our federal securities laws, including statements regarding events or developments that we believe or anticipate will or may occur in the future. These forward-looking statements are subject to a number of risks and uncertainties, including those set forth in our SEC filings, and actual results may differ materially from any forward-looking statements that we make today.

These forward-looking statements speak only as of the date that they are made, and we do not assume any obligation to update any forward-looking statements except as required by law. With that, I'd like to turn the call over to Julie.

Julie Sawyer Montgomery:Thank you, Rachel, and good morning, everyone. Before we get into the quarter, I'd like to share my perspective on Danaher today and the opportunity ahead as I begin this next chapter as CEO. The opportunity for Danaher is straightforward: to become the defining leader in Life Sciences and Diagnostics, a company that unambiguously gains share, delivers sustainable, profitable growth, and helps our customers improve outcomes for patients around the world. The foundation we built at Danaher is strong. We operate leading businesses, foster deep customer relationships, and empower talented people, all enabled by the Danaher Business System. At the same time, growth over the past several years has not consistently reflected the full potential of our portfolio.

We've navigated significant changes in our markets, but regardless of the environment, we hold ourselves to a higher standard. We see a meaningful opportunity to accelerate sustainable core revenue growth, gain share more consistently, and more fully translate the strength of our portfolio into differentiated performance. I'm confident in what we've built, and I'm energized by what I've seen across Danaher these last few months. Our focus now is strengthening execution and delivering on that potential. Recently, I had a conversation with one of our executives preparing for a customer meeting related to Alzheimer's disease.

What started as a discussion about how one of our businesses could help address a particular part of that customer's challenge quickly expanded to cover the roles seven different operating companies could play across discovery, AI-enabled target selection, laboratory automation, process development, scale-up, and diagnostic testing. When the challenge is Alzheimer's disease, speed matters, both to the scientists working to understand it and the families waiting for answers. That conversation reinforced something important. Our customers don't think about their challenges through the lens of our organizational structure. They have a problem to solve, and they want the best partnership and solutions we can bring them.

I see this as critical to Danaher's next chapter, as some of our greatest opportunities sit at the intersections of our businesses. We will preserve what makes our operating company structure advantage, the customer intimacy, the accountability, while making it easier to bring the full power of Danaher to our customers. Our foundation and the power of the Danaher Business System have given us leadership positions across the Life Sciences and Diagnostic markets and a unique role in helping accelerate the translation of scientific discovery into human impact. Our Life Science businesses enable discovery, our Biotechnology businesses help turn those discoveries into scaled and accessible therapies, and our Diagnostics businesses help guide treatment.

Together, Danaher spans a broad path from experiment to patient with DBS adding speed and operating discipline at scale. We call that innovation at the speed of life, helping close the distance between human need and the science that answers it. As we enter this next chapter, we'll accelerate that ambition by focusing on four strategic priorities: commercial excellence, innovation, talent, and effective capital allocation. Each is important, but our most immediate opportunity is commercial execution. Danaher has successfully repositioned its portfolio with three platforms across the Life Sciences and Diagnostics markets. With that portfolio transformation largely complete, our focus is shifting from reshaping the portfolio to delivering more growth from the businesses we own.

We will focus our leadership attention on exceptional commercial execution, enhancing our pursuit of unambiguous share gain across Danaher. We will drive consistency and rigor and commercial execution across our businesses. This means simplifying and strengthening our commercial processes and empowering our leaders to make more entrepreneurial decisions. We also have an opportunity to make it easier for our customers to take advantage of the full power of Danaher. Our operating companies have important brands and deep customer relationships. These will remain fundamental to how we compete, but Danaher has tremendous scale and breadth, and we can do more to use that advantage. That means making the broader strength of our portfolio and capabilities more accessible to customers.

We have already taken practical steps to show up as a more connected Danaher. In Diagnostics, for example, we are successfully deepening customer relationships by bringing leaders from across our businesses together with key customers to look across the portfolio, better understand their priorities, and identify where a more coordinated approach can create additional value. We do this by having our key Diagnostics leaders in the same room at the same time with our key customers to understand their biggest pain points and where we can drive incremental value. This approach has generated meaningful incremental revenue opportunities and is helping drive share gains across our Diagnostics businesses.

As we bring more of Danaher to our customers, we can also become more systematic about connecting capabilities across our businesses to solve more customer needs. Aldevron and Cytiva's recent collaboration to deliver an end-to-end mRNA solution is a great example, helping streamline our customers' development processes while meaningfully accelerating timelines. Ultimately, our commercial strategy is straightforward. Execute better and more entrepreneurially, show up together as Danaher for our customers, and connect our capabilities where we can create greater value. We will make it easier for customers to access the full strength of Danaher and look to us when trying to solve their most important challenges. Our second priority is delivering more innovation.

Danaher is already at the forefront of innovation, but I believe strengthening our innovation capabilities represents one of our largest opportunities to accelerate long-term growth. Delivering on our brand promise, innovation at the speed of life, means we will be deliberate and strategic about where we invest in R&D and ensure we appropriately allocate resources behind our best ideas. That means more closely linking strategy and R&D investments, concentrating resources behind the highest potential initiatives, and working more closely across our businesses and external partners to move promising innovations faster. We will also fund transformational opportunities at the enterprise level when we believe Danaher has a clear right to win and larger investment can create meaningful competitive advantage.

These decisions will require clear choices and greater enterprise-level conviction about where we can create the most value. Innovation cycles take time, but over the long term, we believe this more focused approach can support higher and more durable core revenue growth while turning more scientific discoveries into meaningful human impact. To me, this is the heart of innovation at the speed of life, helping promising science move faster towards the patients who need it. Our third priority is being the home and destination for exceptional talent. We believe our ability to attract and develop exceptional talent in scientific, AI, commercial, and operating disciplines will increasingly set us apart from competitors.

We also need to develop and deploy our people more intentionally against Danaher's highest priority growth and innovation opportunities. Danaher has given me that kind of exposure in my own career, learning DBS and then applying it across commercial, R&D, and business leadership. I want us to continue to create exceptional opportunity for the next generation of leaders. As we evolve DBS for the AI era, I believe we can create an even more compelling place for the best talent in our industry. Our fourth priority is being more disciplined with our capital and resources. M&A and capital deployment have been essential drivers of Danaher's growth and will remain so.

We will maintain the robust investment criteria that has served us well for many decades while bringing strategic clarity and discipline to how we allocate capital and resources. We are focused on deepening our positions in attractive markets and identifying strategically compounding areas that build from the strengths we already have in our businesses. Our objective is to deliver high returns on our investments with greater consistency while positioning Danaher for sustainably differentiated and profitable growth. Across each of these priorities, there is a common idea. We create more value by building a stronger, more connected company. That doesn't mean changing what makes our operating companies successful.

It means preserving their customer intimacy and accountability while making it easier to share ideas, capabilities, talent, and resources across Danaher, and using our scale where it gives us an advantage. AI is one capability we believe can help us do just that. We believe the combination of AI and DBS will be an important competitive advantage. DBS gives us a common way to solve problems, improve processes, and scale what works across Danaher. We believe that approach can help us bring AI solutions to life faster and more effectively than many.

Over time, we believe AI can make DBS simpler and more powerful while DBS can help us implement AI with the rigor and consistency that have long defined Danaher. We see opportunities for AI to strengthen commercial execution and innovation. For example, helping our teams identify opportunities earlier, improve sales funnel management, and dramatically reduce R&D timelines. AI can help simplify work and drive greater productivity. AI isn't only about making Danaher better. It is also changing the needs of our customers and creating new opportunities across our portfolio. For example, we see growing demand for solutions that cut across our Life Sciences businesses that enable more automated and autonomous labs and workflows.

We also see longer-term opportunities across our Biotechnology and Diagnostics platforms to make therapies more efficiently and make treatment decisions more precisely. This is why we are accelerating AI deployment across the enterprise and establishing AI partnerships. Stepping back, we believe a more connected Danaher with a stronger focus on commercial excellence, innovation, and talent can be a stronger Danaher. We intend to bring the best of Danaher to our customers to better leverage our talent, platforms, and brand, and simplify how we operate so our teams can focus on the opportunities that matter most. Together, these actions can help us move faster and more fully realize the potential of our portfolio. I am incredibly excited about what lies ahead.

We are starting from a position of strength with meaningful room to deliver more. That will take time, and we know credibility will be earned through results. Our focus now is making clear choices about where we invest and executing with greater speed and consistency. We believe that can accelerate profitable growth, drive share gains, and most importantly, help our customers improve outcomes for patients around the world. With that, let me turn to our third quarter results. Our third quarter came in ahead of our expectations on both the top and bottom line, with Biotechnology, Life Sciences, and Diagnostics core revenue, excluding respiratory revenue, all growing mid-single digits or better.

Core revenue growth, excluding respiratory revenue, improved to 5.5%, and we delivered a nearly 30% adjusted operating profit margin. These results reflect both improved end market conditions and the benefit of strong commercial and operational execution across the portfolio. We're particularly encouraged by the improved momentum we saw across our businesses. Underlying demand across large pharma and biopharma remained robust. Biotech activity continued to strengthen. While academic demand remained below historic levels, demand improved sequentially. Meanwhile, clinical and applied end markets remained healthy and continued to perform well. Having spent considerable time with our teams over the past several weeks, I've seen firsthand the talent, innovation, and customer focus that make Danaher unique.

Let me walk you through a few notable examples from across Danaher this quarter. During a recent visit to Cytiva's site in Uppsala, Sweden, I had the opportunity to spend time with the teams developing and manufacturing some of our industry-leading products. Seeing firsthand the depth of science and engineering behind these technologies reinforced my confidence in our competitive position. I was particularly impressed by the process development team and how closely that team works side by side with customers to solve their most difficult challenges. That partnership has long been important in traditional monoclonal antibodies, and it becomes even more valuable as our customers move towards more complex molecules and modalities.

We're bringing innovation and process expertise to help customers solve those challenges, and importantly, we're seeing that differentiated approach help us win more specifications with customers. Next, we recently announced our first AI-powered autonomous lab. Based at Abcam, this lab brings together AI, robotics, and technologies from across our portfolio, including Cytiva, Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, Genedata, IDT, and Molecular Devices, to offer a connected design, make, and test workflow.

By continuously learning from each experiment, the platform is designed to help researchers move from idea to validated reagent up to eight times faster, while generating up to ten times higher volume compared to existing models, helping accelerate scientific discovery while providing the rigorous quality and reproducibility required to advance AI-driven drug discovery. Our partnership with NVIDIA, announced last week, will further advance this vision by connecting our instruments and workflows with NVIDIA's capabilities to help shape autonomous science for our customers. On the capital allocation front, Leica Biosystems closed the acquisition of StatLab in early Q4.

StatLab strengthens Leica's value proposition by enabling a more complete pathology workflow while advancing our integrated delivery network strategy and helping clinicians diagnose cancer faster and more precisely. We're very pleased to welcome the StatLab team to Danaher. Finally, Masimo, our other recent acquisition, continued to track ahead of our initial expectations and delivered another quarter of high single-digit revenue growth. Having spent time with the team just last week, the integration is progressing well across the business with a healthy funnel of cost savings and commercial synergy opportunities.

The team has also continued to innovate at an impressive pace, recently receiving FDA clearance for its smartSET platform that can help detect atrial fibrillation, a common heart rhythm disorder that often goes undetected and significantly increases the risk of stroke. This technology can help patients earlier who may benefit from further medical evaluation and care. I want to congratulate the Masimo team for their sixth FDA clearance this year and for extending the value of their technology beyond monitoring to help detect important clinical conditions like atrial fibrillation. With that, I will turn the call over to Matt, who will walk you through our Q3 results and guidance in more detail.

Matt Gugino:Thanks, Julie, and good morning, everyone. As Julie stated, we delivered a solid third quarter with better than expected growth, earnings, and cash flow. Sales were $6.6 billion and core growth, excluding respiratory revenue, was up 5.5%, an encouraging 100 basis points acceleration from the second quarter and a continuation of the improvement we have seen throughout the year. Respiratory revenue, while slightly better than expected, represented an approximately 250 basis point headwind in the quarter, resulting in core revenue growth of 3%. Geographically, core revenues in developed markets were flat. Western Europe grew mid-single digits and North America was down low single digits, primarily driven by lower respiratory revenue.

Core revenues in high growth markets increased approximately 10% with healthy growth across all major regions. China was up high single digits with growth in all three of our segments. Biotechnology and Life Sciences were supported by healthier funding and investment levels, and Diagnostics continued to move beyond the most significant impacts of China's healthcare policy changes. Our gross profit margin for the third quarter was 58.5%. Our adjusted operating profit margin of 29% was up 110 basis points and exceeded expectations, driven primarily by strong operational execution with a modest benefit from tariff refunds received during the quarter. Adjusted diluted net earnings per common share of $2.11 were up approximately 11.5%.

We generated $1.6 billion of free cash flow in the quarter and $4 billion in the first three quarters of the year, resulting in a year-to-date free cash flow to net income conversion ratio of 128%, further underwriting the differentiated quality of our earnings. Now turning towards our business segments. Core revenue in our Biotechnology segment increased 5%. Core revenue in discovery and medical decreased low single digits with solid growth in protein research instrumentation more than offset by timing and lab consumables. Core revenue in bioprocessing grew towards the upper end of mid-single digits, modestly better than our expectations. Consumables were up mid-single digits, led by upstream consumables, while equipment increased low single digits.

Orders grew mid-teens in the quarter, with particular strength in both upstream consumables as well as reagents. There is no change to our full year expectation of mid-single digit core revenue growth from bioprocessing. Demand trends remain healthy across the business, supported by strong commercial production activity and a robust pipeline of new programs. These underlying market trends, combined with Cytiva's differentiated portfolio, deep scientific expertise, and recent innovations, reinforce our confidence in the business' ability to deliver sustainable high single digit long-term revenue growth while helping customers improve yields, increase manufacturing efficiency, and scale new therapies. Turning to our Life Sciences segment, core revenue increased 4.5%.

Core revenue in Pall's applied filtration business increased mid-single digits, driven by continued robust growth in aerospace and microelectronics. Core revenue in our Life Sciences instruments businesses increased mid-single digits in the quarter. SCIEX led the way with strong demand from pharma and biopharma customers, a modest improvement in U.S. academic spending, and continued momentum for new products such as ZenoTOF 8600. Beckman Coulter Life Sciences also delivered strong results, including in automation, where the team has seen increased demand for AI-enabled solutions and services.

Core revenue in our Life Sciences consumables businesses collectively grew low single digits in the quarter, driven by continued momentum in IDT's MRD and next generation sequencing product lines, while Abcam saw improved academic demand and solid traction from pharma and biopharma commercial initiatives. Moving to our Diagnostic segment, core revenue growth excluding respiratory revenue was up 7%. Respiratory revenue was an approximately 650 basis point headwind in the quarter, resulting in core revenue growth of 50 basis points. Core revenue in our clinical Diagnostics businesses increased mid-single digits in the quarter. We saw notable performance at Leica Biosystems, with particular strong momentum in digital pathology as well as advanced staining.

Beckman Coulter Diagnostics also delivered its highest core growth quarter in more than two years. The traction we saw from new product introductions, including the DxI 9000, together with easing China policy related headwinds, reinforces our confidence in Beckman's competitive position and ability to accelerate their growth trajectory. In molecular diagnostics, core revenue in Cepheid's non-respiratory business increased low double digits, led by growth in group A strep, virology, and sexual health assays. Respiratory revenue was approximately $350 million in the third quarter, down year-over-year, due primarily to lower global infection rates, but modestly ahead of our expectations as we saw customers purchase ahead of the upcoming respiratory season.

Now let's turn to our fourth quarter and full year 2026 outlook and give you an initial perspective on how we're thinking about 2027. In the fourth quarter, we expect core revenue growth excluding respiratory revenue to be in the 4%-5% range. We expect respiratory revenue to be an approximately 150 basis point headwind. Additionally, we expect a fourth quarter adjusted operating profit margin of approximately 29.5%. For the full year 2026, we are increasing our full year adjusted diluted net EPS guidance to $8.57-$8.62 versus our prior range of $8.45-$8.60. This reflects the benefit of our third quarter outperformance and represents double digit year-over-year EPS growth.

Turning to 2027, while it's still too early to provide a formal outlook, we want to give you some perspective on how we're thinking about core growth next year. We're encouraged by the improvement in the end markets and the growth we've delivered throughout 2026. Excluding respiratory revenue, core revenue growth has averaged 4%-5% over the past several quarters. As we look to 2027, we think that 4%-5% core revenue growth, excluding respiratory revenue, is the right starting point as we sit today. We will provide a more quantitative and detailed guidance outlook in January, but hopefully this gives you a helpful starting point for how we are thinking about next year.

With that, I will turn the call back over to Julie.

Julie Sawyer Montgomery:Thanks, Matt. To wrap up, we are pleased to deliver better than expected third quarter results and encouraged by the improving growth trends we saw across the business. As I reflect on my first few weeks as CEO, the time I have spent with our teams and customers has only strengthened my conviction in the solid foundation Danaher has built. My focus now is simple: create more value for customers, accelerate innovation, attract and develop great talent, and deploy capital in ways that strengthens Danaher for the long term. These priorities are designed to drive faster and more durable core growth, deliver unambiguous share gains, and more fully translate the strength of our portfolio into differentiated performance.

While realizing the full potential of these opportunities will take time, I am confident that with DBS as our foundation, we are uniquely positioned to turn those opportunities into results for our customers and the patients they serve, our associates, and our shareholders. I am excited about what we can accomplish together and the results we can deliver as we continue building an even stronger Danaher. With that, I will turn the call back over to Rachel.

Rachel Vatnsdal:Thanks, Julie. That concludes our formal comments. We are now ready for questions.

Operator:Thank you, Rachel. At this time, if you would like to ask a question, please press star one on your keypad. To leave the queue at any time, please press star two. We ask that you please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. Once again, that is star one to ask a question. Our first question will come from Doug Schenkel with UBS. Please go ahead.

Doug Schenkel:Hi. Good morning. Thank you for taking my questions. Julie, welcome to the call. As the new CEO, you are new to the role, but as we all know, you are certainly not new to Danaher. Recognizing that, and also that this has been a challenging period for the company, but also that Danaher has a legacy of operational excellence and solid capital deployment, how are you balancing the legacy of a company that has business school case studies written about its strategy and execution versus the opportunity and need to make change? Essentially, as you sit here today, what is foundational, and how do you think about evolving the playbook?
